description: The plot illustrates how classification accuracy (ACC) varies with co-occurrence number for multiple methods (Base, FT, IKE, MEND, a purple-labeled method, and ROME). The x-axis is labeled “Co-occurrence Number,” uses a logarithmic scale with major ticks at approximately 10, 100, and 1000, and spans from near 0 up to several thousand (the plotted points appear around ~5, ~30, ~300, and ~3000). The y-axis is labeled “ACC (%)” on a linear scale ranging from 60 to 85, with regularly spaced tick labels every 5 percentage points (60, 65, 70, 75, 80, 85). The Base line is black with circular markers and a solid line, increasing from about 64% at the smallest co-occurrence to about 71% at the largest, with intermediate points near ~66.5% and ~69%. The FT line is blue with downward-triangle markers and a solid line, rising from about 65% to about 73% across the x-range (around ~69% and ~71.5% at intermediate points). The IKE line is red with upward-triangle markers and a solid line, increasing from about 67.5% to about 75% (around ~72% and ~74.5% mid-range). The MEND line is brown with diamond markers and a solid line, moving upward from about 70.5% to about 80% (around ~75.5% and ~78.5% at intermediate x-values). The purple line (hexagon markers, solid) increases from about 69.5% to about 77.5% (around ~74% and ~77% mid-range). The ROME line is green with square markers and a solid line, increasing from about 74.5% at the smallest co-occurrence to about 84% at the largest, with intermediate values near ~79.5% and ~82.5%.
